before_taxonomy.classification_basis: The malicious Python release used the Mistral SDK package identity. The repository advisory identifies no matching release tag, commit or workflow and says the upload bypassed the normal publishing pipeline. The attributed package origin therefore differed materially from the supported contribution history. This affected developer trust and reuse. A genuine distribution endpoint does not make the attacker’s contribution an authorised Mistral release. This finding is bounded to that Python release; valid workflow provenance elsewhere in the campaign does not prove code safety or establish the same publishing route here. Mistral withdrew the compromised SDK versions within hours. The Python project was also quarantined. These measures acted on the identified malicious distribution and limited further availability through the affected release channel. This establishes a bounded protective effect for release containment. It does not establish customer credential recovery, removal from private caches or the effectiveness of every earlier safeguard. Aikido’s detection need not be proved to have caused Mistral’s action to assess the withdrawal itself.

evidence_search.notes: Current screen reads the repository-preserved source-attributed evidence and complete episode inventory. It does not claim fresh full-text access to every originating source. No canonical restamp or independent source verification is implied.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Mistral says the TanStack worm compromised a developer device and led to malicious SDK releases. Its investigation found no impact to global infrastructure.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The developer-device pathway must remain distinct from global compromise.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Compromised npm SDK versions were published on 11 May and removed early on 12 May. PyPI mistralai 2.4.6 was published and removed on 12 May. Trusted package identities carried attacker content.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Package provenance substitution and payload execution are different questions.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The PyPI version ran malicious code on Linux import and launched a detached credential-harvesting process. The repository advisory specifies imports under mistralai.client on Linux; a bare namespace import does not trigger the loader.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Reported payload behaviour does not quantify actual stolen credentials.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The updated advisory says the compromised npm releases referenced a missing file, so their malicious path could not run. It still instructed users to remove them.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A compromised release is distinct from a working payload.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Aikido separately detected malicious npm versions. Mistral removed its affected releases within hours, but the public accounts do not link one operative Mistral control to detection and withdrawal. The repository advisory also records quarantine of the Python project. That protective action can be assessed separately from the causal route connecting the external detection to provider withdrawal.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: External detection and provider removal must retain their separate causal limits.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Mistral marked mitigation on 13 May and closed its investigation on 14 May. It advised affected users to clean systems, rotate accessible secrets and review cloud logs and retained package copies.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Advised downstream remediation is distinct from confirmed completion at every customer.

episode_inventory.purpose: Present source-backed material actions and later responses in supported relative order. Separate runs, source attributions and unknown ordering remain explicit.

notes: G01 role-scope hold: the sufficient-effect/independent-downstream-harm exclusion overlaps the bounded positive quarantine finding. Preserve that role. Missing npm file is a defective malicious payload, not proof of an effective intentional safeguard; Linux client imports differ from bare namespace imports.

failure_recognition.condition: An output, record, statement, contribution, or artefact is attributed to a specific actor or source.
failure_recognition.assessment: Malicious releases appeared under trusted Mistral SDK identities.

failure_recognition.condition: Available lineage does not support that attribution or supports a materially different attribution.
failure_recognition.assessment: The code came from a compromise rather than an authorised Mistral change.

failure_recognition.condition: The attribution difference is material to interpretation, accountability, recognition, authority, or reuse.
failure_recognition.assessment: Package identity affected installation trust and execution.

success_recognition.condition: An output has materially distinct human, generated, retrieved or transformed contribution roles.
success_recognition.assessment: Software was distributed under publisher/package source identity.

success_recognition.condition: Published attribution reflects the evidenced origins and contribution roles with explicit uncertainty where appropriate.
success_recognition.assessment: The attacker content was not accurately distinguished from legitimate releases.

success_recognition.condition: Comparison of the output's attribution with its contributing records confirms proportional representation of those roles.
success_recognition.assessment: The advisory identifies the compromised versions and invalid source premise.

exclusions.condition: A source is merely omitted where attribution is not material.
exclusions.assessment: The trusted package identity is an affirmative source representation.

exclusions.condition: The attributed actor or source genuinely supplied the relevant material.
exclusions.assessment: The malicious release was not an authentic approved change.

exclusions.condition: The issue is factual inaccuracy unrelated to who supplied or created the material.
exclusions.assessment: The problem is release origin, not only incorrect program output.

failure_recognition.condition: A defined governance or protective control is applicable and validly becomes operative.
failure_recognition.assessment: The Python project was quarantined after the malicious release.

failure_recognition.condition: The control has an identifiable protective purpose requiring a material effect such as prevention, blocking, containment, interruption, redirection, limitation, escalation, mitigation, or another protection-compatible outcome.
failure_recognition.assessment: Quarantine restricts further distribution through that project route.

failure_recognition.condition: The actual control effect materially falls short of that required protective purpose, allowing the governed hazard to be delivered, continue, escape containment, or remain insufficiently mitigated.
failure_recognition.assessment: The reported quarantine supplies the bounded distribution restriction; existing local copies are a separate residual pathway.

failure_recognition.condition: The shortfall is material in the evidenced hazard and protection context; where vulnerability, developmental status, capacity limitation, temporary or situational consent impairment, acute distress, cognitive asymmetry, or another heightened protection condition is relied on, that condition must itself be supported rather than presumed.
failure_recognition.assessment: No shortfall in that narrow quarantine effect is established.

success_recognition.condition: An applicable validly activated protective control faces its governed hazard.
success_recognition.assessment: The malicious Python release faced an activated project quarantine.

success_recognition.condition: The control produces a timely effect sufficient for its protective purpose and evidenced context, including any justified heightened protection.
success_recognition.assessment: Quarantine bounded subsequent project distribution for the identified package route.

success_recognition.condition: Observed intervention and hazard outcome demonstrate the required containment or mitigation rather than activation alone.
success_recognition.assessment: The advisory reports the actual project quarantine, not only a detection alert.

exclusions.condition: The applicable control does not become operative when a valid activation condition occurs; assess Required Control Activation.
The control becomes operative even though its valid activation or applicability conditions are not satisfied; assess Control Activation Validity.
exclusions.assessment: The malicious release supplied valid applicability.

exclusions.condition: The control becomes operative with a sufficient effect but its operative state is later lost, weakened, reset, or transformed before reaching the governed point; assess Control-State Preservation.

An operative governance signal fails to reach any capable endpoint or execution surface; assess the applicable governance-control reach class rather than treating non-delivery as inadequate control effect.
exclusions.assessment: The action reached the package distribution surface.

exclusions.condition: The control produces the protective effect required by its defined purpose and the remaining harm arises through an independent downstream mechanism.
exclusions.assessment: The scoped distribution effect does not remove existing installed copies, whose residual risk is a separate downstream mechanism.

exclusions.condition: The dispute is solely that policy should have required a stronger safeguard, without evidence of an applicable operational control or protective-effect obligation in the material context.
exclusions.assessment: An actual quarantine action is evidenced.

exclusions.condition: Disability, neurodivergence, diagnosis, age-associated stereotype, or another personal characteristic is used by itself to presume incapacity, vulnerability, or diminished agency.
exclusions.assessment: No personal characteristic is relied on.
